label: Fire risk
title: Estimated chance of fire (experimental)
subtitle: 28 Sep to 2 Oct 2026
source: Tinga Lens model on NASA SMAP, FIRMS, VIIRS and CHIRPS data
how: Each district shows the estimated chance that satellites record at least one fire in it during 28 Sep to 2 Oct 2026. The estimate comes from a statistical model (logistic regression) fitted to fires since 2015. It combines how often the district burned on these dates in other years with how far surface and root-zone soil moisture, the speed of drying, and lagged rainfall and greenness are from their usual values for the time of year.
limits: This is an experimental model, not a fire warning. Do not use it for safety decisions.
Tested on years it was not trained on, the model scored AUC 0.93 (0.5 is chance, 1 is perfect) and improved on the seasonal pattern alone by 2% (Brier skill).
Adding root-zone moisture to surface moisture changed the prediction error by +0.1% and gave a better score in 4 of 13 test years.
Temperature, humidity and wind are not included, so short hot, dry, windy spells are missed.
A fire here means a satellite detection. Small or short fires are missed, and most detections are seasonal farm and bush burning.
Larger districts have a higher chance simply because there is more land to burn.
